annotations.title: Connect an account with a sign-in form

description: Connect an account that signs in with a form instead of a browser sign-in: any mailbox over IMAP/SMTP (platform "imap": email, password (an app password where the provider has them), imapHost, smtpHost; optional imapPort (993), smtpPort (465), username (default: email), name), Bluesky ("bluesky": handle, appPassword), Telegram ("telegram": botToken, chatId), Inkwire ("inkwire": siteUrl, apiKey, name) or a business bank account on PI-SPI, the BCEAO instant payment system ("pispi": participant (bank code, e.g. BJB999), clientId, clientSecret, apiKey from the bank's Business API; optional paymentAddress, accountNumber, name; for a live account apiBaseUrl, tokenUrl, certificate and privateKey (PEM, the BCEAO-issued mTLS client certificate), else the BCEAO sandbox) or a PayPal business account ("paypal": clientId, clientSecret, email; optional currency, name, environment) or an n8n instance ("n8n": baseUrl, apiKey; optional name, webhookUrl) or Bing Webmaster Tools ("bing-webmaster": apiKey from Bing Webmaster → Settings → API access; optional name) or a new phone number for texts and AI calls ("phone": country US or CA; optional areaCode, name. This BUYS a number: $3.00 a month from the Anaella balance, so get the user's yes first) or a Stripe account by its restricted key ("stripe": apiKey (rk_live_…); optional name; Stripe can also connect through its sign-in page with a connect link). Anaella checks the login first and stores nothing if it fails; the error says what to fix. Use only details the user gave you for this. If they would rather not share a password with you, send them to https://anaella.com/channels?connect=<platform> to enter it themselves. Every other account type (Google, Microsoft, Slack, Meta…) needs a browser sign-in: use the connect link from find, or create_connect_link. Returns the new channel; use its id as channelId.
